title: papio AcquisitionBundle v2
description: bundle.json for one ready job. Identical to acquisition-bundle/1 except that the accepted candidate may carry an entitlement object recording the route by which access was obtained. A new schema rather than a v1 addition because v1 sets additionalProperties:false and papio rejects unknown fields recursively, so a v1 consumer would reject the whole document. Never contains API keys, cookies, signed query values, or identity-provider URLs; unknown fields are rejected (fail closed).

evidence.description: Human-readable identity evidence, e.g. 'doi 10.x found on page 1 text'.

reuse_license.description: SPDX-ish license or 'unknown'. Distinct from access_basis: downloadable never implies redistributable. Read together with entitlement.acquisition_mode: the mode says a credential or session was used, the license says which terms apply, and (daemon_held_credential, 'unknown') is a real pair meaning papio used a licensed API but never learned its terms.

entitlement.description: How access was obtained. A route, never an identity: papio never authenticates a human and never holds institutional credentials. Omitted entirely when no route was observed; no field is filled by inference.

route.description: Bare origin only: scheme and host, with no path, query, fragment, or userinfo. This is the origin the artifact was retrieved FROM. It is not an assertion that papio sent a credential to that host — for a licensed API the credential may go to the API service while the file comes from the publisher. landing_url is unsuitable because it retains its query string.

entitlement_ref.description: Which entitlement, never a secret and never a credential instance. Rotating an API key does not change it, so no rotation semantics may be built on this field. Omitted when papio observed no entitlement.

acquisition_mode.description: Derived from access_basis: open_access -> open_access; licensed_api -> daemon_held_credential (the acquisition was authorised by an API credential papio holds). institutional and manual yield NO entitlement object at all, so operator_browser_session is currently a reserved value with no producer: the only writer of institutional is browser adoption, which records that basis for every adopted download including an open-access file the browser fetched, so asserting it would invent evidence for a route nobody walked.
